subject: biology

items.q: Do animal cells have a cell wall?
items.correct: No — only plant cells (and bacteria/fungi) have a cell wall.
items.misconception: Yes, all cells have a cell wall.
items.random_wrong: Only red blood cells have a cell wall.
items.why: Animal cells have a membrane but no wall; plant cells have a cellulose wall for support.

items.q: Does diffusion require energy from the cell?
items.correct: No — diffusion is passive and needs no energy.
items.misconception: Yes, diffusion uses energy like active transport.
items.random_wrong: Diffusion only happens in dead cells.
items.why: Diffusion moves particles down a concentration gradient passively; active transport (against the gradient) needs energy.

items.correct: Most cells do; very active cells like muscle have many.
items.why: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration, so cells needing lots of energy have more of them.

items.q: Are all cells in an organism identical?
items.correct: No — cells are specialised (differentiated) for their functions.
items.misconception: Yes, every cell is exactly the same.
items.random_wrong: Only plants have different cell types.
items.why: Cells differentiate into types like nerve, muscle and red blood cells, each suited to its job.
